html:
Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was an Indian jurist, economist and Dalit leader who chaired the committee that drafted the Constitution of India. He lived from 1891 to 1956.

He was born into the Mahar caste, treated as "untouchable", and faced exclusion at school. He still earned doctorates in economics from Columbia University in New York and the London School of Economics, and trained as a barrister in London. Few Indians of any caste did so much study abroad in the 1920s.

His life's work was the fight against caste:

  • He led the Mahad Satyagraha of 1927, when Dalits drew water from a public tank closed to them.
  • He clashed with Gandhi over separate electorates for Dalits. The Poona Pact of 1932 gave reserved seats instead.
  • As the first law minister in Nehru's cabinet he steered the Constitution, which abolished untouchability, and pushed the Hindu Code Bills on marriage and inheritance. He resigned in 1951 when they stalled.

Late in life he decided Hinduism could not be reformed from within. In October 1956 in Nagpur he became a Buddhist with several hundred thousand followers, the mass conversion that began the Dalit Buddhist movement. He died seven weeks later. Today he is one of the most honoured figures in India, and his statues stand in villages across the country.
